sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794

items.q: Fill up: The three autoimmune causes of chronic tubulointerstitial disease listed are sarcoidosis, Sjögren's syndrome and ______ disease.
items.exp: Etiology item 7 (autoimmune): sarcoidosis, Sjögren's and IgG4 disease, followed by item 8, CKD of unknown etiology (CKDu). (Book p794)

items.q: Fill up: The last entry in the etiology list of CTID is CKDu, which stands for CKD of ______.
items.exp: Etiology 8: CKD u (unknown) — CKD of unknown cause, discussed later as CKDu. (Book p794)

items.q: CTID is described as having which onset?
items.exp: Features of CTID: asymptomatic, insidious onset — hence patients often present late. (Book p794)

items.q: A patient with CTID has polyuria and nocturia. The table explains this by:
items.exp: Clinical-features table: polyuria and nocturia arise from a defect in concentration capacity. (Book p794)

items.q: Anaemia in chronic tubulointerstitial disease is caused by damage to:
opts: Erythropoietin produced from peritubular interstitial fibroblasts
Erythropoietin produced by the glomerular mesangium
Erythropoietin produced by the proximal tubular brush border
items.exp: Anaemia row of the table: erythropoietin is produced from peritubular interstitial fibroblasts, which are damaged in CTID. (Book p794)

items.q: Match the tubular lesion with the resulting syndrome in the table — 1) Cortical collecting duct fibrosis  2) β cell fibrosis  3) α intercalated cell fibrosis … A) RTA I  B) RTA IV/pseudohypoaldosteronism (↓Aldosterone action)  C) Nephrogenic DI (↓ADH action)
items.exp: Clinical-features table: cortical collecting duct fibrosis → ↓ADH action = nephrogenic DI; β cell fibrosis → ↓aldosterone action = RTA IV (pseudohypoaldosteronism); α intercalated cell fibrosis → RTA I. (Book p794)

items.q: A patient with CTID has hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis and low aldosterone effect, and is labelled as pseudohypoaldosteronism. Which lesion and type of RTA is this?
opts: β cell fibrosis causing RTA IV
α intercalated cell fibrosis causing RTA I
Cortical collecting duct fibrosis causing nephrogenic DI
items.exp: RTA IV (pseudohypoaldosteronism) results from β cell fibrosis with ↓aldosterone action; RTA I results from α intercalated cell fibrosis. (Book p794)

items.q: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus in CTID is due to fibrosis of the cortical collecting duct reducing ADH action.
opts: False — it is due to central ADH deficiency
False — it is due to α intercalated cell fibrosis
items.exp: Table: nephrogenic DI — cortical collecting duct fibrosis → ↓ADH action. (Book p794)

items.q: A child with CTID has severe rickets. The table attributes this to:
items.exp: Children with CTID develop severe ricketic features due to loss of PO₄³⁻. (Book p794)

items.q: Match each CKD condition with its anaemia severity in the book's note — 1) CTID  2) ADPKD  3) Reason ADPKD has the least anaemia … A) EPO production is preserved  B) Minimum anaemia  C) Maximum anaemia
items.exp: Note on anaemia in CKD: maximum in CTID and minimum in ADPKD, because EPO production is preserved in ADPKD. (Book p794)

items.q: Among the causes of CKD, CTID is associated with the maximum anaemia and ADPKD with the minimum.
opts: False — ADPKD has the maximum anaemia
False — anaemia is equal in all causes
True, but only after dialysis starts
items.exp: Note: anaemia in CKD — maximum in CTID, minimum in AD-PKD. (Book p794)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed autoimmune causes of CTID. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Autoimmune list for CTID: sarcoidosis, Sjögren's and IgG4 disease; anti-GBM disease causes RPGN. (Book p794)
